title: The Internal Auditor Who Found WorldCom's Hidden Billions

lines.say: May two thousand two. WorldCom's CEO, Bernard Ebbers, has just resigned.
lines.show: May 2002. WorldCom's CEO, Bernard Ebbers, has just resigned.

lines.say: Inside the company, the internal audit department finds billions in expenses booked as capital.
TIME reported that its head, Cynthia Cooper, and her team worked late into the night, in secret.
On June eleventh, according to TIME, the CFO asked her to delay the audit. She refused, and went to the board's audit committee.
lines.show: On June 11, according to TIME, the CFO asked her to delay the audit. She refused, and went to the board's audit committee.

lines.say: June twenty-fifth, WorldCom disclosed the fraud. Within twenty-four hours, the S.E.C. sued.
lines.show: June 25, WorldCom disclosed the fraud. Within 24 hours, the SEC sued.

scene.src: DOJ Corporate Fraud Task Force, 2003 · SEC complaint, Jun 26, 2002

lines.say: The stock lost ninety percent. The CEO got twenty-five years.
lines.show: The stock lost 90%. The CEO got 25 years.

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
